title: PLL Jitter Wars
tagline: Jitter accumulation compares four phase-tracking strategies under increasing noise and loop bandwidth.

curves.label: Type-I PLL
curves.code: let jitter=0; for(let k=1;k<=n;k++){ jitter += 0.4/Math.sqrt(k) + 0.02 + 0.7/(1+k); } return jitter/5;
curves.name: Type-I PLL

curves.label: Type-II PLL
curves.code: let jitter=0; for(let k=1;k<=n;k++){ jitter += 0.25/Math.sqrt(k) + 0.01 + 0.6/(1+k); } return jitter/5;
curves.name: Type-II PLL

curves.label: Kalman Phase Tracker
curves.code: let x=0; for(let k=1;k<=n;k++){ let gain=0.12/Math.sqrt(k); x += gain + 0.005; if(k%5===0) x += 0.03*Math.exp(-k/80); } return x;
curves.name: Kalman Phase Tracker

curves.label: Bang-Bang PLL
curves.code: let jitter=0; for(let k=1;k<=n;k++){ let s = (k%2===0)?1:0.7; jitter += (0.18/Math.sqrt(k))*s + 0.02 + 0.9*Math.pow(Math.log(1+k),1.2)/(1+k); } return jitter/5;
curves.name: Bang-Bang PLL

curves.label: Dead-Zone PLL
curves.code: let jitter=0; for(let k=1;k<=n;k++){ let dz = (k<120)?Math.exp(-k/120):0; jitter += 0.3/Math.sqrt(k) + 0.006 + 0.2*dz*k/120 + 0.5/(1+k); } return jitter/5;
curves.name: Dead-Zone PLL
